template.tagline: Light two small hybrids, climb past 100 km, come home.
template.brief: Two small hybrid motors, fins for stability and a small science box. A hybrid burns a solid fuel grain with a liquid oxidizer, so it pushes gently for a long time instead of all at once: the rocket climbs through the thick air slowly, keeps the air load and the g low, and coasts up past the 100 km line that is commonly used as the edge of space. There is nothing to stage.

benchmark.text: Sounding rockets are short research flights: up, a few minutes of data or weightlessness, then down. A long, low-thrust burn keeps max-Q and acceleration modest, which is kinder to the payload than a short, violent solid burn. 100 km is the altitude commonly used as the boundary of space.

review: Hybrid motors (2× hybrid-small, 25 kN each at sea level) burn about 80 s; peak air load about 38 kPa and peak acceleration about 7 g. 1,750 kg of propellant peaks about 102 km in the flown sim: inside the ±5% band around the 100 km target, and still past the 100 km line.
